info.title: AutoX API
info.description:
Vehicle marketplace API. Headless and API-first: this document is the whole contract, and the Angular web app and a future native mobile app consume exactly these endpoints.

**Conventions that apply everywhere:**

* **Money** is an integer in the currency's minor unit, with an ISO 4217 code beside it. `priceAmount: 1850000, priceCurrencyCode: "EUR"` is €18,500.00. The scale comes from `GET /api/v1/reference/countries`.
* **Distance** is always kilometres on the wire, whatever a market displays.
* **Errors** are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`. Branch on `code`, never on `detail` — `detail` is English developer text and is not translated. Validation failures add a flat `errors` array of `{field, message}`.
* **Enums** serialise as their constant name. The full set a client may receive is at `GET /api/v1/reference/enums`; display labels are the client's own responsibility.
* **List endpoints are cursor-paginated.** Pass the previous response's `nextCursor` back as `cursor`. There are no page numbers and no total count.
* **Images are never uploaded through this API.** Request a slot, PUT the bytes straight to object storage with the pre-signed URL, then confirm.

post.summary: Turns a description such as "SUV diesel automatique moins de 15 000 €" into the filters GET /api/v1/listings takes
post.description:
Turns a description such as "SUV diesel automatique moins de 15 000 €" into the filters GET /api/v1/listings takes. Does not search: apply criteria and search as usual.

Only the query is sent to the language model, and every value it returns is checked against our enums, the catalogue and fixed bounds; what fails, and what the search cannot filter on, is listed in notUnderstood.

404 when the feature is off. 429 RATE_LIMITED beyond ten requests in ten minutes from one address. 503 INTERPRETER_UNAVAILABLE when the model times out (five seconds), its quota is spent or it fails — then use the ordinary search.

post.summary: Reports a message the caller received to the moderators.
post.description:
Reports a message the caller received to the moderators. Once per message: reporting it
 again is accepted and changes nothing. A message cannot be edited or deleted, by anyone.

post.summary: Changes the password
post.description:
Changes the password. Requires the current one, even though the request is already authenticated: a valid token may be a stolen one, and taking over the account permanently is the most valuable thing that can be done with it.

Returns a new token pair, and invalidates every existing session including the caller's. The client must store the tokens from this response; the refresh token it arrived with no longer works. An access token carries no reference to the session it was issued with, so "all sessions but this one" is not something the server can express — replacing the lot is the version of that guarantee it can actually keep.

get.summary: Search the live listings
get.description:
Search the live listings. Every filter is optional; no filters means everything visible.

Paginated by cursor, not by page number: nextCursor from one response is cursor in the next. There is no page number, because offset paging over a table being written to skips and repeats rows. The number of matches is a separate call, GET /api/v1/listings/count, so that no page pays for it.

post.description: Creates a DRAFT. Publication is a separate, explicit call.

post.description:
Writes to a listing's seller. Starts the caller's conversation about it, or continues it
 if they already have one. 404 if the listing is not online and the caller has no
 conversation about it yet; 403 for the caller's own listing.

post.summary: ACTIVE to PAUSED.
post.description: ACTIVE to PAUSED. Keeps the listing and its photos, frees the quota slot.

post.summary: ACTIVE or PAUSED to SOLD, recording the outcome.
post.description:
ACTIVE or PAUSED to SOLD, recording the outcome. Seller only; a sold listing stays
 visible to its owner and drops out of public search.

post.description: Extends the expiry window, and revives an expired listing.

post.summary: DRAFT, PAUSED or EXPIRED to ACTIVE.
post.description: DRAFT, PAUSED or EXPIRED to ACTIVE. Checks the active-listing cap.

post.summary: Marks every message in the conversation read for the caller.
post.description: Marks every message in the conversation read for the caller.

post.summary: Writes in a conversation.
post.description: Writes in a conversation. 409 once it is closed: see canReply.

post.summary:
Creates an account and signs it in, returning the same token pair as login — so a
 client never has to follow registration with a second call
post.description:
Creates an account and signs it in, returning the same token pair as login — so a client never has to follow registration with a second call.

role chooses PARTICULIER or PROFESSIONNEL; a professional must also send companyName and registrationNumber. ADMIN cannot be self-assigned.

post.summary: Exchanges a refresh token for a new pair.
post.description:
Exchanges a refresh token for a new pair. The old refresh token is invalid
 afterwards — clients must store the one returned here.

post.summary: Sets a new password using the token from a reset link
post.description:
Sets a new password using the token from a reset link.

The link works once and only for a short window. Every way it can fail — unknown, expired, already spent, replaced by a newer request — answers 400 INVALID_RESET_TOKEN, because a legitimate user does the same thing in all four cases: ask for a new link.

A successful reset ends every session on every device. The user signs in again.

post.summary:
Asks for a password reset link, which is emailed to the address if it belongs to an
 account that can use one
post.description:
Asks for a password reset link, which is emailed to the address if it belongs to an account that can use one.

Always 202, and always the same body, whether or not the address is registered: anything else would turn this into a way to find out who has an account here. The caller therefore cannot tell from the response that anything was sent. Repeated requests answer 429 RATE_LIMITED — the address does not have to be one the caller owns, so the endpoint is capped both per account and per caller.

post.summary: Ends this device's session.
post.description: Ends this device's session. Idempotent: an unknown token still returns 204.

post.summary: Exchanges credentials for a short-lived access token and a long-lived refresh token
post.description:
Exchanges credentials for a short-lived access token and a long-lived refresh token.

A wrong password and an unknown address both answer 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS, deliberately indistinguishable. Repeated failures answer 429 TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS with Retry-After; the delay is progressive and capped, so failing on purpose cannot lock the real owner out.

post.summary: Hides the message from both sides (its text is kept) and closes its reports.
post.description: Hides the message from both sides (its text is kept) and closes its reports. 409 if already dealt with.

post.summary: Closes the report and leaves the message as it is.
post.description: Closes the report and leaves the message as it is. 409 if already dealt with.

post.description:
Takes down a listing that is online. Reversible — see {@link com.autox.admin.AdminListingController#reinstate #reinstate} — unlike a
 seller's own delete. A reason is required.

post.summary: Refuses a listing awaiting review; it leaves the site.
post.description: Refuses a listing awaiting review; it leaves the site. A reason is required.

post.summary: Brings back a listing a moderator refused or took down.
post.description:
Brings back a listing a moderator refused or took down. It returns online, or
 paused if the seller's quota is full, or expired if its window has run out.

post.summary: Accepts a listing awaiting review.
post.description: Accepts a listing awaiting review. 409 if it is not online and unreviewed.

get.summary:
The signed-in account: contact details, role, country, locale and — for a
 PROFESSIONNEL — the company profile.
get.description:
The signed-in account: contact details, role, country, locale and — for a
 PROFESSIONNEL — the company profile. Never another user's; the id comes from the
 token, not from the request.

patch.summary: Partial update: only the fields present in the body are changed.
patch.description:
Partial update: only the fields present in the body are changed. Email and role are
 not editable here — changing an address needs to prove control of the new one, and
 changing a role is a commercial decision, not a profile edit. The password has its
 own endpoint below.

get.summary:
One listing, as a buyer sees it: full description, equipment codes and the image gallery
 in order, each image with its three size variants
get.description:
One listing, as a buyer sees it: full description, equipment codes and the image gallery in order, each image with its three size variants.

404 unless the listing is ACTIVE, not rejected, not soft-deleted and not past its expiry — including when the caller happens to be its owner, who reads it at /api/v1/listings/mine/{id} instead. The VIN, the seller's email and the exact coordinates are not part of this response.

delete.summary: Soft delete: the row stays for the audit trail but disappears from every read.
delete.description: Soft delete: the row stays for the audit trail but disappears from every read.

patch.summary: Partial update of a listing the caller owns
patch.description:
Partial update of a listing the caller owns. Only the fields present in the body change.

status is not among them: state changes go through their own endpoints, which is what makes the transition rules unbypassable. Editing an ACTIVE listing is allowed and keeps it live.

get.summary:
An estimate of a car's value: the median asking price of comparable live listings,
 each brought to this car's age and mileage, with the interquartile range around it
get.description:
An estimate of a car's value: the median asking price of comparable live listings, each brought to this car's age and mileage, with the interquartile range around it.

The comparables are the price indicator's: same model, same fuel, power within 15 %, registered within two years, in the same mileage band. With fewer than five there is no estimate, and widerScopes lists the loosenings that would give one; ask again with one as scope. 404 for an unknown model.

get.summary:
The engines of a model that are listed now, each a fuel and a power with the version name
 sellers most often give it: the choices a visitor values a car with.
get.description:
The engines of a model that are listed now, each a fuel and a power with the version name
 sellers most often give it: the choices a visitor values a car with. 404 for an unknown
 model.

get.summary: Which optional search features this server has.
get.description: Which optional search features this server has. A client hides natural-language search when interpret is false.

get.summary: Vehicle manufacturers
get.description:
Vehicle manufacturers.

Empty until the catalogue is seeded; listings identify their vehicle by free text in the meantime, and the search endpoint accepts a name as well as an id for that reason.

get.summary: The model lines of one manufacturer.
get.description: The model lines of one manufacturer. 404 if the make is unknown.

get.summary: The equipment vocabulary: code, category and display order, with the seeded labels.
get.description: The equipment vocabulary: code, category and display order, with the seeded labels.

get.summary: Every enum value the API may return or accept, keyed by type name
get.description:
Every enum value the API may return or accept, keyed by type name.

Values only. Display labels belong in the client's own translation files; what a client must not duplicate is the set of constants.

get.summary:
The open markets: default locale, currency and the currency's minor-unit scale, which a
 client needs in order to render the integer prices this API returns.
get.description:
The open markets: default locale, currency and the currency's minor-unit scale, which a
 client needs in order to render the integer prices this API returns.

get.summary: Every live session, newest first
get.description:
Every live session, newest first.

Not paginated, and the one list endpoint in the API that is not. The bound is how many devices one person signs in from, which is single digits: a page parameter here would be ceremony around a list that cannot grow.

The response cannot say which entry is the caller's own. An access token carries no reference to the refresh family it was issued with, so a client that wants to mark one as "this device" should match on the deviceLabel it chose at sign-in.

get.summary:
"Annonces similaires": three to six live listings like this one, best first, as search
 result cards; an empty list when there are fewer than three good matches, never padding
get.description:
"Annonces similaires": three to six live listings like this one, best first, as search result cards; an empty list when there are fewer than three good matches, never padding.

The same model registered within three years and priced within 40 % first, then the same body type within 20 % of the price. Never the listing itself, and at most one of a seller's copies of the same car. 404 when the listing is not public, as for the detail.

get.summary: The seller's own listings, in every state.
get.description: The seller's own listings, in every state. Paginated; there is no unbounded form.

get.summary: How many listings the caller has online and how many they may have
get.description:
How many listings the caller has online and how many they may have.

A private seller is capped; a dealer is not, and limit is then null. Use it to explain the cap before the seller tries to publish — the cap itself is enforced by POST /listings/{id/publish}, which answers 409 ACTIVE_LISTING_LIMIT_REACHED whatever this said a moment earlier.

get.summary: How many listings match the same filters GET /api/v1/listings takes
get.description:
How many listings match the same filters GET /api/v1/listings takes.

Exact up to 10 000; beyond that capped is true and count is the cap, to be shown as "more than 10 000". The bound keeps the cost constant however large the catalogue grows. Call it once when the filters change — not per page — and do not make the result list wait for it.

get.summary: The caller's conversations, as buyer and as seller, most recent first.
get.description: The caller's conversations, as buyer and as seller, most recent first.

get.summary: One conversation with its latest messages.
get.description: One conversation with its latest messages. Reading it does not mark it read; that is POST /conversations/{id/read}, so a GET changes nothing.

get.summary: How many conversations have a message the caller has not opened.
get.description: How many conversations have a message the caller has not opened. For the header badge.

get.summary: Up to eight makes and models whose name starts with q, ignoring case and accents: "citro" finds Citroën, "a3" the A3, "audi a" the Audi A1, A3, A4… Makes come first, then the most listed.
get.description: Up to eight makes and models whose name starts with q, ignoring case and accents: "citro" finds Citroën, "a3" the A3, "audi a" the Audi A1, A3, A4… Makes come first, then the most listed. Only entries with a listing online are returned; none is an empty list. 400 if q is shorter than two characters or longer than sixty.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What has been typed: 2 to 60 characters.

get.summary: Accounts, newest first, optionally filtered by role
get.description:
Accounts, newest first, optionally filtered by role. Paginated by page number rather than by cursor: this is an operator tool over a slowly growing table, where jumping to a page is worth more than the consistency a cursor gives.

Closed accounts are excluded. Password hashes are never included.

get.summary: Open reports, oldest first.
get.description: Open reports, oldest first.

get.summary: One of the three moderation lists, a page at a time.
get.description: One of the three moderation lists, a page at a time. PENDING is the queue: online and not yet reviewed, oldest first.

get.summary: One listing in any state, with its moderation trail.
get.description: One listing in any state, with its moderation trail. 404 once its seller has deleted it.

delete.description:
Ends one session. The device holding it can no longer refresh, and its access token stops working when it expires — within fifteen minutes, which is the cost of a stateless API and the reason that lifetime is short.

A session belonging to someone else, or one already ended, answers 404: there is nothing to be learned here by guessing identifiers.

delete.summary: Removes the photo, its variants and the stored objects, and closes the ordering gap.
delete.description: Removes the photo, its variants and the stored objects, and closes the ordering gap.

ReorderImagesRequest.description:
The gallery's new order, front to back. Position 0 is the cover photo.

Must be a complete permutation of the listing's ready images — a partial list is rejected rather than interpreted, because "move this one to the front" and "these are the only ones I know about" are indistinguishable otherwise, and guessing wrong silently reorders someone's gallery.

ImageResponse.description:
One photo as the API exposes it: an id, its place in the gallery, and a URL per variant.

Storage keys are not exposed. A client that knew them could construct URLs we did not issue, and changing bucket layout would then be a breaking API change.

VariantView.description: Dimensions travel with the URL so a client can reserve layout space before loading.

InterpretRequest.description: A visitor's description of the car they want, in their own words.

query.description:
at most 200 characters: a sentence, not a document. It is the only thing sent
              to the language model.
query.example: SUV diesel automatique moins de 15 000 € en bon état

InterpretResponse.description: A natural-language search, as filters the listing search accepts.

criteria.description: the filters, exactly as GET /api/v1/listings takes them: catalogue ids, prices in the currency's minor units with the currency beside them. Every value has been checked; none comes straight from the model.

summary.description: what was applied, in French, for display: "SUV · Diesel · Automatique · ≤ 15 000 €". Written by the server from criteria, so it never describes a filter that is not there.

notUnderstood.description:
the parts of the request that could not become a filter — something the
                      search cannot filter on ("bon état", a colour) or a value that failed
                      checking (a make not in the catalogue). Empty when everything was used.

ListingSearchCriteria.description:
Everything a buyer can filter on. Every field is optional; an empty criteria object means "all visible listings".

Make and model can each be given two ways, and both are needed:

  • makeId matches the catalogue exactly — precise, and what the frontend's dropdown will send once the catalogue exists.
  • make matches the displayed name, catalogue row or free text. Until the catalogue is seeded, every listing identifies its vehicle by text, so an id-only filter would match nothing at all.

PriceLevel.description:
Where a listing's price sits against comparable listings. See {@link MarketPrice MarketPrice} for what
 "comparable" means and where the lines are drawn.

MessageReportReason.description: Why a recipient reported a message. Mirrors ck_message_report_reason. A closed list for the reason moderation reasons are one: a code can be counted, and shown in the moderator's language.

ReportMessageRequest.description: note is required when the reason is OTHER, and optional otherwise.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: Password change for a signed-in account.

currentPassword.description:
proof that the caller is the owner and not the holder of a stolen
                        access token

newPassword.description: same single rule as registration: length, no composition theatre

deviceLabel.description:
label for the session this call establishes, since the change ends
                        every existing one. Omitted, the new session is simply unlabelled.

AuthResponse.description:
What login and refresh return.

expiresInSeconds is included alongside the absolute instant so a client with a skewed clock can still schedule its refresh correctly.

UserSummary.description: The compact user shape embedded in auth responses.

CreateListingRequest.description:
A new listing. Created as a DRAFT; nothing here publishes it.

Two either/or rules are enforced before the request reaches the service, mirroring the database's own constraints:

  • Vehicle: each of make and model is given either as a catalogue id or as text, never both and never neither. A trim requires a model.
  • Location: either a gazetteer place id, or postal code plus city as text while the gazetteer is unavailable.
Numeric bounds repeat the table's CHECK constraints so a bad value is a 400 with a field name rather than a 500 from the driver.

EmissionClass.description: Mirrors ck_listing_emission_class. Drives low-emission-zone filters in FR/DE.

ExteriorColor.description: Searchable colour family. Mirrors ck_listing_exterior_color. The manufacturer's own colour name goes in Listing.colorText.

ListingResponse.description:
The owner's view of a listing. Includes the states and timestamps a seller needs to understand what will happen next, and allowedTransitions so a client can render exactly the buttons that will work rather than guessing the state machine.

The public buyer-facing shape will be narrower — no VIN, no moderation detail — and arrives with search.

ListingStatus.description:
Seller-facing lifecycle, and the authority on which moves between states are legal. Mirrors ck_listing_status.

The transition table lives here rather than in the service so there is exactly one definition of what is allowed, and an illegal move is rejected rather than quietly applied. It describes every move the API can make and no move it cannot. Whether a quota permits a move is a separate question, answered by the service. 

   DRAFT ──publish──▶ ACTIVE ──unpublish──▶ PAUSED ──publish──▶ ACTIVE
                        │                     │
                        ├──▶ SOLD ◀───sold────┘
                        ├──▶ EXPIRED ──renew──▶ ACTIVE
                        └──▶ REMOVED ──reinstate (moderator only)──▶ ACTIVE | PAUSED | EXPIRED

Out of REMOVED is a moderator's move, never a seller's. A listing reaches REMOVED two ways. A seller's delete also stamps deleted_at, and the row then exists for no read path at all: it is gone. A moderator's refusal or takedown sets REMOVED alone, and that listing can be reinstated — by a moderator. The seller it belongs to still sees it, and must not be able to put it back online themselves, which is why {@link com.autox.listing.ListingStatus#sellerTargets #sellerTargets()} exists beside {@link com.autox.listing.ListingStatus#allowedTargets #allowedTargets()}.

LocationView.description: resolved is false while the location is still unmatched free text.

ModerationStatus.description: Admin verdict, independent of {@link ListingStatus ListingStatus}. Mirrors ck_listing_moderation_status.

VehicleView.description: fromCatalogue is false when the vehicle is identified by free text.

ImageUploadRequest.description:
Asks for a pre-signed upload URL.

The declared size is not a courtesy: it is signed into the URL, so storage rejects an upload of any other length. That is what stops a client from announcing a 2 MB photo and then pushing 2 GB through a URL we handed it.

ImageUploadTicket.description:
Everything a client needs to upload one photo, and nothing about our storage layout.

The client PUTs the bytes to uploadUrl with exactly requiredHeaders, then calls the confirm endpoint with imageId. The bytes never touch the API.

SendMessageRequest.description: One message. Plain text: it is shown as typed, never as markup.

ConversationDetail.description: A conversation with its messages, oldest first.

earlierOmitted.description: true when the conversation has more messages than are returned (MessagingService.MESSAGES_SHOWN); the oldest are left out

ConversationRole.description: Which side of a conversation the caller is on.

ListingRef.description: The listing the conversation is about, as it is now.

online.description: whether it can be found and opened by the public at the moment

coverUrl.description: its first photo, small; null when it has none

body.description: null when a moderator hid the message

reportedByMe.description: whether the caller has reported it; a message can be reported once

Party.description: The other side: a display name and whether it is a trade seller.

RegisterRequest.description:
Registration payload.

role accepts PARTICULIER or PROFESSIONNEL only — ADMIN is created out of band and can never be self-assigned through this endpoint.

RefreshRequest.description:
The refresh token travels in the body, not in a cookie: a native app has no
 cookie jar, and the same contract has to serve both clients.

token.description: the value from the emailed link's token parameter

ForgotPasswordRequest.description:
Asks for a reset link.

The address is validated for shape only. Whether it belongs to an account is not reported back, by design — see PasswordResetService.

ModerationDecisionRequest.description:
Why a listing is being refused or taken down.

The reason is required: a listing that disappears without one cannot be explained to its seller or defended in a dispute. The note is the moderator's own words, kept for other moderators, and required only when the reason is OTHER.

reasonCode.description: Why. Shown, translated, to the seller.

note.description: Internal detail for other moderators. Required when reasonCode is OTHER.

ModerationReason.description:
Why a moderator refused a listing or took it down. Stored by name in moderation_action.reason_code.

A closed list rather than free text, for two reasons. The seller is told the reason, and a code can be said in their language where a moderator's note cannot. And "how many listings were refused as duplicates last month" is a question a code answers and a sentence does not.

Codes are stable: one that has been written to the trail is never renamed or removed, only retired from the screens that offer it.

ModeratedListing.description:
A listing as a moderator sees it: everything needed to judge it, in one answer.

The whole listing rather than a summary — description, VIN, every photo — because the point of the queue is to decide without opening anything else, and a moderator who has to click through to read the description will stop reading descriptions.

seller.description: who is selling, including the email a buyer never sees

allowedActions.description:
what this listing's state permits a moderator to do — the answer
                       to "would you accept this?", so that no client keeps its own copy
                       of the rules

trail.description: every moderation action on this listing, oldest first

editedSinceReview.description: true when the listing is awaiting review again: it had been approved or reinstated, and its seller has since changed its content. The trail then ends in a decision that no longer stands, and this is what says why.

ModeratedSeller.description: The seller, as an administrator may see them.

ModerationActionType.description: Mirrors ck_moderation_action. REJECT and REMOVE require a reason code.

ModerationEntry.description:
One line of a listing's moderation trail: who did what, when, and why.

Admin-only. It names the moderator and carries their internal note, neither of which a seller is shown — a seller sees the reason code, on their own listing, and no more.

ModerationNoteRequest.description:
The optional body of an approval or a reinstatement: a note for the trail, nothing else.
 Neither needs a reason code — putting a listing online is the unremarkable outcome.

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
Partial profile update. A null member means "leave unchanged"; a blank string clears an optional field.

Email and password are deliberately absent. Changing an email has to re-trigger verification, and changing a password has to revoke every other session — both are their own endpoints, not a field in a profile PATCH.

UserProfileResponse.description:
The full own-profile view. The password hash and the internal version counter are
 not represented here at all, so they cannot leak by accident.

UpdateListingRequest.description:
Partial update. null means "leave unchanged".

Status is not a field here: moving between states goes through the publish, unpublish, renew and delete endpoints, which is what makes the transition rules impossible to bypass. Nor is the seller — a listing never changes hands.

Vehicle and location identification may be switched between catalogue reference and free text, but only coherently: supplying a makeId clears makeText and the reverse, and supplying both is rejected.

ValuationRequest.description:
The car a visitor wants valued, as query parameters.

Only what chooses comparables or adjusts their prices: the catalogue model, the engine (fuel and power), the first registration and the mileage. The gearbox and the version name are not here on purpose: the price indicator does not compare on them, and La Cote values a car the way the indicator judges one, so the two never disagree about the same car.

scope.description: the price indicator's rule, or one loosening of it; EXACT when absent

currency.description:
the currency to value in, which is the currency of the comparables; EUR
                 when absent

ValuationScope.description:
Which comparables La Cote valued a car against: the price indicator's rule, or that rule loosened one way when the car has too few comparables under it.

Each loosening drops or widens one condition, never two, so a buyer reading "toutes motorisations" knows exactly what the figure no longer accounts for.

Valuation.description:
La Cote's answer for one car: an estimate with its range, or the plain statement that there is not enough to estimate from, and in either case what it rests on.

Every amount is an asking price on AutoX, in the currency's minor unit, brought to the car's age and mileage. It is not what cars sell for, which is usually a little less.

scope.description: the comparables rule used: the price indicator's, or one loosening

minimumComparables.description: below this, no estimate is given

estimate.description: null when there are fewer than minimumComparables

basis.description: the comparables actually found; null when there are none

widerScopes.description:
when there is no estimate: the loosenings that would give one,
                           with how many they find. Empty otherwise

ValuationBasis.description: The years and mileages of the comparables found, as listed, before any adjustment.

ValuationEstimate.description: The median of the adjusted prices, with the middle half of them either side: a quarter of the comparables are priced below lowAmount and a quarter above highAmount. Each is rounded to the nearest hundred: a valuation to the euro would claim a precision it does not have.

ValuationWindow.description: The conditions the comparables met. mileageToKm is null for the open-ended top band; the mileage and power bounds are null when the scope does not match on them.

ValuationEngine.description:
One engine of a model as it is listed on AutoX: a fuel and a power, with the version name
 sellers most often give it, and how many live listings have it.

exampleVersion.description:
the most common version text among those listings, which may name a
                       trim level as well as the engine; null when none gave one

SearchCapabilities.description: Optional search features, and whether this server has them.

Model.description: yearFrom/yearTo bound the year filter; null means unknown or current.

Feature.description:
One item of equipment.

code is the identity and the only thing other endpoints exchange. labels is keyed by BCP 47 tag — fr-FR and en are seeded. A client that wants a locale with no row falls back to the language-only tag, then to en, then to the code; the endpoint returns what exists rather than guessing.

FeatureCategory.description: Mirrors ck_vehicle_feature_category. Groups equipment in the listing form and detail page.

Enums.description:
Every enum a client has to map, keyed by the name the API documents it under.

The values, not the labels. Display text belongs in the frontend's own translation files — there is no translation table for enums and inventing one would put French strings in a database that is never the right place to edit them. What the frontend cannot safely duplicate is the set of constants, and that is what this returns: a value appearing here that the frontend has no translation for is a visible gap, where a hardcoded list silently omits it.

Country.description:
An open market.

No localised country name: code is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 value, and a browser renders it in the user's own language with Intl.DisplayNames better than a seeded string could. name is the endonym, for logs and admin screens.

currencyMinorUnit is the one field a price-rendering client cannot do without: every amount in this API is an integer of the minor unit, and dividing by the wrong power of ten is off by a hundred.

SessionResponse.description:
One live session of the signed-in account.

id is the rotation family, not the token row. A session's token is replaced on every refresh, so the row id would change under the client between two reads of the list; the family is stable for the life of the session and is what the revoke endpoint takes.

Nothing here is a credential. The token itself is not in the database in a usable form at all, let alone in this response.

id.description: the session identifier, to pass to DELETE /me/sessions/{id}

deviceLabel.description: what the client called itself at sign-in; null if it said nothing

userAgent.description: raw User-Agent header, for a client that wants to name the device itself

ipAddress.description: where the session was created from, so an unexpected one is noticeable

lastUsedAt.description: when it last refreshed; null if it never has

expiresAt.description: when it dies on its own

SearchSort.description:
The orderings public search supports.

Each one is a keyset sort, so each needs a column that is non-null on every visible listing, plus id as a tie-breaker to make the order total. Without the tie-breaker two listings at the same price would have an undefined relative order, and a cursor sitting between them would either skip or repeat rows.

CursorPagePublicListingSummary.description:
A page of search results.

No total count on the page, deliberately. Counting the matches for an arbitrary filter combination on every page would cost more than the page itself. The count is its own endpoint — GET /api/v1/listings/count, see {@link ResultCount ResultCount} — asked once per filter change and bounded by a cap, so it is off the pagination path entirely.

PriceIndicator.description:
How a listing's price compares with the market, and what the comparison rests on.

Absent (null on the listing) when there is nothing honest to say: fewer comparable listings than the threshold, a new car, or a vehicle not identified from the catalogue. The median and the count are given with the level so a buyer can see what it is based on — "Bonne affaire" with no evidence behind it is a sales pitch.

level.description: the stable code; the frontend words it

medianPriceAmount.description:
median price of the comparable listings, in minor units of the
                          listing's currency

comparableCount.description:
how many listings the median was taken over, the listing itself
                          not included

PublicListingSummary.description:
One result card.

Every enumerated value is the stable code, never a display string: "DIESEL", not "Diesel" and certainly not "Gazole". The French frontend maps codes to French; nothing here assumes a language.

No seller contact details, no VIN, no moderation state. A search result is public, and a scraper gets exactly what a buyer's screen shows.

SellerCard.description: What a buyer sees about who is selling: a name and whether it is a trade seller.

PublicListingDetail.description:
The buyer-facing detail page.

Narrower than the seller's own view of the same listing. Absent on purpose: the VIN (identifies the vehicle and indirectly its owner), the moderation state (an internal matter), the exact coordinates, and anything about the seller beyond a display name.

As in the summary, every enumerated value is a stable code and every feature is a code. There is no human-readable label anywhere in this response.

SellerView.description: role tells a buyer whether this is a dealer or a private sale. demo says the seller is one of the demo seed's accounts, which nobody signs in to, so a message to them will not be answered. Nothing more.

ListingSummary.description:
The row shape for a seller's listing list. Narrow on purpose: a dashboard with fifty
 rows should not carry fifty VINs and fifty descriptions over a mobile connection.

PageResponseListingSummary.description:
The envelope every list endpoint returns.

Spring's own Page serialises its internal structure, which would tie the public contract to a Spring Data version. This is our shape, and it is the only one a mobile client has to understand.

Offset paging is correct for admin tables. Public search will use a keyset cursor instead — same envelope, with a nextCursor added — because offset paging skips and repeats rows while listings are being inserted underneath.

ListingQuota.description:
How many listings the caller has online, against how many they may have.

The rule is enforced when a listing is published, whatever a client believes; this exists so that a client can say so before the seller has spent ten minutes on a listing they will not be allowed to put online.

active.description: listings currently online — the only ones that count

limit.description: the most this account may have online, or null for no limit

canPublish.description:
whether one more could go online now. Advisory: publishing checks
                   again, under a lock, and is the only answer that counts

ResultCount.description: How many listings match a search.

count.description: the number of matches, never more than the cap

capped.description: true when there are more matches than count — the client shows "more than count" rather than the figure itself

ConversationSummary.description:
One line of an inbox.

The other party is a display name and a role, never an email or a phone number: a buyer and a seller reach each other only through these conversations.

role.description: which side the caller is on

unreadCount.description: messages from the other party the caller has not opened

canReply.description:
false once the listing has been taken down or deleted, or either
                    account is closed or suspended; the conversation stays readable

preview.description: the start of the message, or null when a moderator hid it

PageResponseConversationSummary.description:
The envelope every list endpoint returns.

Spring's own Page serialises its internal structure, which would tie the public contract to a Spring Data version. This is our shape, and it is the only one a mobile client has to understand.

Offset paging is correct for admin tables. Public search will use a keyset cursor instead — same envelope, with a nextCursor added — because offset paging skips and repeats rows while listings are being inserted underneath.

UnreadCount.description: How many of the caller's conversations have a message they have not opened.

CatalogueSuggestion.description:
One entry under the search bar as the visitor types: a make, or a model of a make.

Ids and slugs both. The slugs are what the search URL carries (marque=audi), the ids what the rest of the API is keyed on. The model fields are absent on a make.

label.description: What to show: the make's name, or the make's and the model's.

listingCount.description: Listings online now. Never zero: an entry with none is not suggested.

PageResponseUserSummary.description:
The envelope every list endpoint returns.

Spring's own Page serialises its internal structure, which would tie the public contract to a Spring Data version. This is our shape, and it is the only one a mobile client has to understand.

Offset paging is correct for admin tables. Public search will use a keyset cursor instead — same envelope, with a nextCursor added — because offset paging skips and repeats rows while listings are being inserted underneath.

body.description:
the text, also when a moderator has hidden it: the moderator is the one
                 person who needs to read it

reported.description: whether this is the message the report is about

PageResponseReportedMessage.description:
The envelope every list endpoint returns.

Spring's own Page serialises its internal structure, which would tie the public contract to a Spring Data version. This is our shape, and it is the only one a mobile client has to understand.

Offset paging is correct for admin tables. Public search will use a keyset cursor instead — same envelope, with a nextCursor added — because offset paging skips and repeats rows while listings are being inserted underneath.

ReportedMessage.description:
An open report, for a moderator: the message, who reported it and why, and the messages around it so it can be judged in context.

A moderator sees a conversation only through a report on it. There is no endpoint that lets an administrator browse conversations nobody has reported.

context.description: up to MessagingService.REPORT_CONTEXT messages either side of the reported one, and it, oldest first

ModerationView.description: The three lists a moderator works from.

PageResponseModeratedListing.description:
The envelope every list endpoint returns.

Spring's own Page serialises its internal structure, which would tie the public contract to a Spring Data version. This is our shape, and it is the only one a mobile client has to understand.

Offset paging is correct for admin tables. Public search will use a keyset cursor instead — same envelope, with a nextCursor added — because offset paging skips and repeats rows while listings are being inserted underneath.

ApiError.description: RFC 9457 problem+json, extended with a stable `code`. Branch on `code`, never on `detail` — `detail` is untranslated developer text.

message.example: must be a well-formed email address

bearerAuth.description: Access token from `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Short-lived (15 minutes); exchange the refresh token at `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` when it expires. Issuer: https://api.autox.local
